Penalty

/PEN-ul-tee/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Penalty means the punishment imposed for breaking a law, rule, or agreement — the specific consequence itself, such as a fine, a suspension, or a prison term

Penalty means the punishment imposed for breaking a law, rule, or agreement — the specific consequence itself, such as a fine, a suspension, or a prison term. The referee gave the visiting team a penalty for having too many players on the field.

Worked Example

The factory paid a heavy penalty for dumping waste into the river — ten thousand dollars for every day it had violated the environmental rules.

The daily fine is the specific consequence imposed on the factory for breaking the law. That concrete punishment — the fine itself — is the penalty.

How Penalty Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

punishment

punishment: a consequence imposed for wrongdoing

fine

fine: a punishment paid in money

sanction

sanction: an official punishment imposed for breaking a rule or law

Antonyms

reward

reward: something given in return for good behavior or achievement

exemption

exemption: official freedom from a rule or its consequences

How Strong Is It? — warning → penalty → sentence

warning vs. penalty

warning vs. penalty: A warning is a caution that carries no real consequence yet, while a penalty is an actual punishment — a fine, a suspension, lost points — that you must bear.

sentence vs. penalty

sentence vs. penalty: A sentence is one of the most serious penalties of all: a court-ordered punishment that can include years in prison.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — pen-

Root — pen-: punishment (Latin poena, from Greek poine)

Suffix — -al

Suffix — -al: adjective-forming: relating to

Suffix — -ty

Suffix — -ty: noun-forming: state, quality, or instance

Put it together

Put it together: Penalty stacks poena ('punishment') with -al and -ty to name the punishment itself. The same root gives us penal, penalize, and penance.

Use the root in a new word: penance

Use the root in a new word: penance: As penance for missing the meeting, Carlos volunteered to write up the notes for the rest of the month.

Root Check

Word Choice

Neutral / legal and everyday

Penalty names the specific consequence itself — the fine, the suspension, the prison term — and it works in courtrooms, contracts, and sports alike. The related adjective form, punitive (a word taught elsewhere in this unit), describes something as intended for punishment; the penalty is the punishment itself.
